headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: n8n’s server-side write/execute defaults can collide with LightZero’s read-only, non-runnable profile; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by LightZero’s lack of I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, network, browser, MCP, or subprocess surfaces, so it cannot ingest n8n output by default. n8n can move workflow data through files and integrations, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond manual handoff, making prompt injection possible mainly via unusual copy-paste or external workflow wiring.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies n8n-generated text into LightZero prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF n8n writes attacker-controlled content into a shared file that LightZero later reads, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Avoid manual copy-paste between systems.
Keep n8n outputs out of any shared prompt files.
Use explicit provenance labels on workflow artifacts.
requires-engineering: add a trusted-format parser between n8n and any downstream agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while n8n can read and write server files and send workflow data to integrations. Leakage from LightZero into n8n is therefore limited, but n8n can still expose whatever workflow data it processes if sensitive inputs are routed through its integrations.
conditions: IF sensitive data is routed into an n8n workflow, that data may flow to connected integrations.
IF LightZero is wrapped by external tooling that adds file or network access, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not route secrets into n8n workflows unless necessary.
Restrict n8n credentials to least privilege.
Review connected integrations before enabling them.
Keep LightZero isolated from shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls on n8n outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero is read-only and non-runnable, but n8n has execute-shell, filesystem write, and broad egress by default. Because n8n also supports shared state across instances, overlapping writes and workflow actions can conflict with any external artifacts LightZero produces or consumes; uncertainty about the exact shared target should escalate rather than down-rank.
conditions: IF n8n workflows write to the same directory or datastore as another process, write conflicts can occur.
IF multiple n8n instances target the same shared state, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Separate n8n storage from any other agent workspace.
Disable Execute Command unless required.
Use per-workflow directories or namespaces.
Add locking around shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate tools and downstream actions, so if it consumes LightZero output as authoritative, errors can cascade into workflow actions. LightZero itself is not an action-taking agent, which limits blast radius, but the pair still supports a default path where generated content can be treated as input without verification.
conditions: IF n8n uses LightZero output as a decision input without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF a workflow node sends emails, updates records, or triggers APIs based on LightZero output, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action node.
Require human approval for high-impact workflow branches.
Log and review LightZero-derived decisions.
Use schema checks on agent outputs.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: LightZero is open-source game-playing software with no stated data residency issues, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores secrets on its server. The pair can therefore create compliance mismatch if regulated data is routed through n8n’s server filesystem or integrations, even though LightZero alone is not the source of the residency problem.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by an n8n workflow, retention and residency obligations apply to that workflow.
IF n8n credentials or secrets are stored on a server in a disallowed jurisdiction, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into n8n.
Keep regulated data out of noncompliant workflows.
Review n8n retention settings and credential storage.
Document jurisdiction for the n8n server.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls.
